files.lesson.md: --- order: 16 unit: lines9 node: AC9M9A03 n4 uses: [AC9M9A03 n1] assumes: [AC9M9A03 n1] connection: meet-halfway title: The midpoint summary: "The midpoint of two points is halfway along the line between them: the average of the x-coordinates and the average of the y-coordinates." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "Two friends live at opposite ends of town and want to meet halfway. Where on the map is halfway?" app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8363 url: http://127.0.0.1:8363/index.html readySelector: "#board" layout: full --- Halfway between two numbers is their average. Halfway between two points is the average of each coordinate. ## Predict: halfway ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to a halfway point on a grid shows who halves each coordinate and who adds them or halves only one." check: type: predict q: "Two friends live at (2, 3) and (10, 9) on a town grid. They meet at the point exactly halfway between their homes. Where do they meet?" options: - "(6, 6)" - "(12, 12)" - "(6, 3)" - "(4, 3)" actual: "(6, 6). Halfway across from 2 to 10 is 6. Halfway up from 3 to 9 is 6." ``` Where is the point halfway between the two homes? ## Run: place the halfway point ```step stage: run insight: "Dragging a point to the middle and seeing equal halves along the line connects 'halfway' with the average of each coordinate." try: { playground: board, starter: "mid.yml#run", height: 560 } check: { type: board, text: "Drag $M$ to the point halfway between $A$ and $B$. Was your prediction right?", when: "x(M) = 6 and y(M) = 6" } ``` Drag $M$ along the line until it's halfway between $A$ and $B$. ## Investigate: averaging ```step stage: investigate insight: "The midpoint's x-coordinate is the average of the two x-coordinates, and its y-coordinate is the average of the two y-coordinates. Adding without halving gives a point far outside the line." tasks: - check: type: number q: "Find the number halfway between $x = 4$ and $x = 12$." answer: 8 explain: "(4 + 12) ÷ 2 = 8." - check: type: question q: "What is the midpoint of $(-2, 5)$ and $(4, -1)$?" options: ["$(1, 2)$", "$(2, 4)$", "$(-1, 3)$", "$(3, 2)$"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "That adds the coordinates and doesn't halve the y: (−2 + 4 = 2, 5 + −1 = 4).", "Check the x: (−2 + 4) ÷ 2 = 1.", "Check the x: (−2 + 4) ÷ 2 = 1."] explain: "x: (−2 + 4) ÷ 2 = 1. y: (5 + −1) ÷ 2 = 2. The midpoint is (1, 2)." smaller: check: { type: "number", q: "What is $(-2 + 4) \\div 2$?", answer: 1, explain: "−2 + 4 = 2, and 2 ÷ 2 = 1." } - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#tam" text: "Tam finds the midpoint of $(2, 3)$ and $(10, 9)$. Click the line where his working goes wrong." answer: 3 fault: logic misconception: midpoint-sum-not-half explain: "Line 3: he stopped after adding. (2 + 10) ÷ 2 = 6 and (3 + 9) ÷ 2 = 6, so the midpoint is (6, 6)." ``` ### Halfway between numbers Here's finding a midpoint. ```worked A(2, 3),\; B(10, 9) :: The two points. x = \frac{2 + 10}{2} = 6 :: Average the x-coordinates. y = \frac{3 + 9}{2} = 6 :: Average the y-coordinates. M(6, 6) :: The midpoint. ``` Now try one on paper: the points $(-4, 1)$ and $(6, 9)$. Find the midpoint, then type its $x$-coordinate. ### Which midpoint? ### Find the mistake Read Tam's working. Which line forgets a step? ## Modify: work backwards ```step stage: modify insight: "Finding an end point from the midpoint reverses the same averaging: the midpoint is as far on one side as the other." try: { playground: board, starter: "mid.yml#vary", height: 560 } tasks: - hint: ["From A to M is 3 across and 4 up.", "Go the same again past M."] check: { type: board, text: "$M$ is the midpoint of $A$ and $B$. Drag $B$ to the right place.", when: "x(B) = 8 and y(B) = 11" } - hint: ["Average the x-coordinates: (x + 8) ÷ 2 = 5.", "So x + 8 = 10."] check: { type: number, q: "The midpoint of $P$ and $(8, 3)$ is $(5, 4)$. What is the $x$-coordinate of $P$?", answer: 2, explain: "(x + 8) ÷ 2 = 5, so x + 8 = 10 and x = 2." } - hint: ["Both points have y = 6."] check: { type: question, q: "Edge case: both points have the same $y$-coordinate, 6. What is the $y$-coordinate of the midpoint?", options: ["6", "3", "12", "0"], answer: 0, feedback: [null, "That halves one 6 only.", "That adds without halving.", "Nothing makes it 0."], explain: "(6 + 6) ÷ 2 = 6: the midpoint is on the same horizontal line." } ``` ### The far end ### The missing coordinate ### The same height ## Practise: find the midpoint ```step stage: practise insight: "Averaging coordinates, with negatives and with the missing end." tasks: - check: type: question q: "Find the midpoint of $(0, 4)$ and $(8, 10)$." options: ["$(4, 7)$", "$(8, 14)$", "$(4, 14)$", "$(4, 3)$"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "That adds without halving.", "Halve the y-coordinates too.", "Add the y-coordinates: 4 + 10 = 14, then halve."] explain: "(0 + 8) ÷ 2 = 4, (4 + 10) ÷ 2 = 7." - check: type: number q: "Find the $y$-coordinate of the midpoint of $(3, -6)$ and $(5, 2)$." answer: -2 explain: "(−6 + 2) ÷ 2 = −4 ÷ 2 = −2." smaller: check: { type: "number", q: "What is $-6 + 2$?", answer: -4, explain: "Start at −6 and go up 2: −4." } - check: type: number q: "The midpoint of $A$ and $B(9, 5)$ is $(6, 4)$. What is the $y$-coordinate of $A$?" answer: 3 explain: "(y + 5) ÷ 2 = 4, so y + 5 = 8 and y = 3." - check: type: question q: "Review: how far is it between $(0, 0)$ and $(6, 8)$?" options: ["10", "14", "48", "7"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "That adds the sides.", "That multiplies them.", "That's the average of 6 and 8."] explain: "6² + 8² = 100, and √100 = 10." ``` ### A midpoint ### The y-coordinate ### Working backwards ### Review From the last lesson: the distance between two points. ## Make: the bus stop ```step stage: make insight: "Returning to the halfway point: place a stop between two places and say what 'halfway' means on the map." tasks: - hint: ["Average the x-coordinates.", "Then average the y-coordinates."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "Two schools are at $(1, 2)$ and $(9, 12)$ on a grid in km. A bus stop goes halfway between them. Find its coordinates, then type the $x$-coordinate." steps: - ["$x = \\frac{1 + 9}{2} = 5$", "average the x-coordinates"] - ["$y = \\frac{2 + 12}{2} = 7$", "average the y-coordinates"] - ["$(5, 7)$", "the stop is at (5, 7)"] answer: "5" answerLabel: "x-coordinate of the stop" tolerance: 0.001 feedback: - ["10", "That adds 1 and 9. Halve it."] - ["7", "That's the y-coordinate. The x-coordinate comes first."] criteria: - "I averaged the x-coordinates and the y-coordinates separately." - "I wrote the midpoint as a pair of coordinates." - "I checked that it's as far from each school." explain: "(1 + 9) ÷ 2 = 5 and (2 + 12) ÷ 2 = 7: the stop is at (5, 7)." - check: type: number q: "What is the $y$-coordinate of the stop?" answer: 7 explain: "(2 + 12) ÷ 2 = 7." - check: type: question q: "Is the stop halfway by road as well?" options: ["Not necessarily: roads aren't straight", "Yes, always", "Only if the schools are the same size"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "The midpoint is halfway in a straight line; roads bend.", "Size doesn't matter."] explain: "The midpoint is halfway along the straight line between the schools. By road it could be further for one of them." ``` ### The stop Back to the bus stop. Work it out on paper first, then type your answer. ### The other coordinate ### By road The schools and grid here are made up for the task. **Also used in** - **Meeting points.** Apps find a fair place for two people to meet by using the midpoint (then check the roads). - **Games.** The centre of a line between two characters is the midpoint of their positions. - **Next lesson.** Using gradient, distance and midpoint together in one problem. ```teacher summary: Students find the midpoint of two points by averaging each coordinate, and work backwards to a missing end point (AC9M9A03, node 4). time: 40 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 12 min · Modify 8 min · Practise and Make 12 min goals: - I can find the point halfway between two points. - I can average the x-coordinates and the y-coordinates separately. - I can find an end point when I know the midpoint. struggle: "Adding without halving. Ask: is the answer between the two points?" before: > Students need Gradient between two points. The one idea: the midpoint is the average of each coordinate. The common mistake is adding without halving (Tam's working): a quick check is whether the answer lies between the two points. The homes and schools are made up for the task. running: - "Predict: take a show of hands. Those who chose (12, 12) added the coordinates." - "Run: ask whether M is on the line and how far from each end." - "Paper: the try-one after the worked example and the bus stop in Make are worked on paper first. Books out, and look for both averages written out." - "Modify: before B moves, ask what the step from A to M is." stuck: - see: A student gets (12, 12) for the midpoint. ask: Is (12, 12) between the two points? fix: "No: halve each sum to get (6, 6)." - see: A student averages x and y together. ask: Which coordinates go together? fix: x with x, and y with y. stretch: Find a point a third of the way from A to B. support: Count squares along the line on a grid and halve the count. leads: > Continues AC9M9A03 node 4. Where it leads: the combined problem next, then coordinate geometry proofs in Year 10. exit: q: Find the midpoint of (2, 6) and (8, 12). a: (5, 9). explain: > The midpoint is halfway between two points. Its x-coordinate is the average of the two x-coordinates, and its y-coordinate is the average of the two y-coordinates. ```
